summary.what: Cal football home games at Memorial Stadium -> Downtown Berkeley, 2023 to 2025. No football was used to measure any curve.
summary.window: 5 hours before kickoff to 7 hours after
summary.attendance_given: last season's average, not the real gate

why: Parking: almost none, even less than Oracle Park, which pushes non-walking fans toward transit. This raises the share.
Walk: 20-25 minutes uphill versus about 15 minutes flat to Embarcadero. This deters some riders, especially older fans and families, and lowers the share.
Crowd type: a large student block walks from campus and never touches BART. Alumni and families from around the Bay lean on BART. Net, this lowers the share relative to a regional MLB crowd.

Competing transit: Oracle has Muni Metro, ferries, Caltrain and several BART stations splitting riders. In Berkeley, DBRK is the main regional rail stop and its only competitors are buses and shuttles. This raises the share strongly and is the main reason the multiplier sits above 1.
Time of day: Saturday evening means no commuters are already on BART and weekend headways are longer. Late-night return frequency slightly discourages BART.
Parking: almost none at Memorial Stadium, even scarcer than Oracle Park, which pushes the BART share up.
Walk: 20 to 25 minutes uphill from Downtown Berkeley, versus a 15-minute flat walk at Embarcadero, which pushes the share down.
Crowd type: a large student share lives within walking distance and does not need BART, which pushes the share down relative to an MLB crowd.

Competing transit: Downtown Berkeley has no Muni rail or ferry alternative, only AC Transit and ride-hail, so BART captures more of the transit riders. This partly offsets the walk and student penalties.
Time of day: a Saturday 13:00 start matches the EMBR day-game reference, so I apply no extra adjustment beyond choosing the day curves.
Parking: Memorial Stadium has almost none, slightly less than Oracle Park's little parking. This is neutral to slightly positive for BART.
Walk: the 20 to 25 minute uphill walk from DBRK is longer and harder than Embarcadero's 15 minute walk, which lowers BART's share.
Crowd type: a large share of students walk from campus housing, and there are few transit-captive tourists. This lowers BART's share noticeably.

Competing transit: DBRK has no Muni or ferry competition, only AC Transit. That diluting effect is part of the Embarcadero share, so BART matters more here for non-walkers. This offsets a substantial part of the penalties.
Time of day: a Saturday noon start matches the reference day games, many of which are on weekends. Lower weekend train frequency is a minor penalty at most.
Parking: the stadium has almost no parking, which is stricter than Oracle Park, so more non-walking fans must use transit. This pushes the share up.
Walk: the 20-25 minute uphill walk is less attractive than Embarcadero's flat 15 minutes. This pushes the share down.
Crowd type: many students live within walking distance and never enter a station. This pushes the share down.

Competing transit: Oracle Park's BART riders split across Embarcadero, Montgomery, Muni, ferries and Caltrain. In Berkeley, Downtown Berkeley is effectively the only rail gateway, so the BART share concentrates there. This pushes the share up strongly and outweighs the two downward factors.
Time of day: the Saturday 19:00 start matches the night-game reference, so there is no adjustment.
Parking: Memorial Stadium has almost no parking, even less than Oracle Park. This pushes non-student fans toward transit and raises the BART share.
Walk: The 20-25 minute uphill walk from DBRK is longer than EMBR's 15-minute flat walk. This trims the share somewhat.

Crowd type: Many students live within walking distance and will not use BART. Alumni and family fans coming from San Francisco and the East Bay are heavy BART users, which partly offsets the student effect.

Competing transit: This is the main reason to go above 1.0. Oracle Park has Muni Metro at the gate plus Caltrain and ferries, so Embarcadero captures only a sliver. DBRK is the only rail option to Memorial Stadium, with only AC Transit buses as a weak competitor.
Time of day: A Saturday 13:00 start matches the day-game baseline, so no extra adjustment. Weekend service and the absence of commuters make BART an easy choice.
Parking: Memorial Stadium has almost no parking, even less than Oracle Park, so more non-student fans are pushed onto transit. This pushes the share up.
Walk: the 20-25 minute uphill walk from Downtown Berkeley is longer and harder than the 15-minute flat walk to Oracle Park. This pushes the share down.
Crowd type: a large student section lives within walking distance and will not use BART at all. This pushes the share down.

Competing transit: Oracle Park riders can choose Muni Metro, Caltrain and ferries. In Berkeley the only real competitor is AC Transit buses, so regional transit riders mostly use BART. This pushes the share up and largely offsets the walk and student effects.
Time of day: a Saturday afternoon kickoff fits the day-game reference, and weekend service is adequate, so no further adjustment.
Parking: the stadium has almost no parking, which is similar to or tighter than Oracle Park, so this factor pushes slightly toward BART.
Walk: the 20 to 25 minute uphill walk from DBRK is longer and harder than the roughly 15 minute flat walk to Oracle Park, so fewer people will choose BART.
Crowd type: a large student share lives within walking distance and never touches BART, which lowers the share against an MLB crowd.
Competing transit: there are no ferries and no Muni-style rail competition, only AC Transit buses, so BART carries more of the transit trips. This partly offsets the walk and student effects.
Time of day: a Saturday afternoon has no commute overlap and matches the day-game reference, so this is roughly neutral.
Parking: the stadium has almost no parking, even less than Oracle Park, which pushes the BART share up.
Walk: the 20 to 25 minute uphill walk from DBRK is longer than the 15 minute walk from Embarcadero, which pulls the share down.
Crowd type: a large student block lives within walking distance and will not use BART, which pulls the share down noticeably.

Competing transit: Oracle Park riders can choose Muni, ferries and other downtown BART stations. Berkeley has only AC Transit buses and a single obvious BART station, so DBRK captures most rail riders. This pushes the share up.
Time of day: Saturday-night service is somewhat less frequent than the weekday-heavy EMBR night sample. This slightly reduces BART use. On balance the share is modestly above EMBR night.
Parking: Memorial Stadium has almost no parking, less than even Oracle Park's limited supply. This pushes non-walking fans toward BART and raises the share.
Walk: the 20 to 25 minute uphill walk is longer and steeper than Embarcadero's 15-minute flat walk. This lowers the share somewhat.
Crowd type: a large student section walks from campus and nearby housing and never touches BART. This lowers the share. The rest of the crowd is regional and has few alternatives.

Competing transit: Embarcadero's share is diluted by Muni, ferries, Caltrain and other downtown SF BART stations. DBRK is the single dominant rail station for the stadium, with only AC Transit buses competing. This is the largest upward factor and outweighs the walk and student effects.
Time of day: this is a Saturday night game, matching the night reference. Pre-game riders arrive in early evening, when few compete with commuters, so no extra adjustment.
Parking: Memorial Stadium has almost no parking. Oracle Park has sizable nearby lots and garages. This pushes BART share clearly above EMBR.
Walk: the walk from DBRK is 20-25 minutes and uphill, against Embarcadero's 15-minute flat walk. This pulls BART share down.
Crowd type: a large student block walks from campus housing and never touches BART. This pulls share down, though non-students still dominate the crowd.
Competing transit: Oracle Park is served by Muni Metro, Caltrain and ferries. Berkeley has only AC Transit buses competing, so BART carries most regional transit trips. This pushes share up.

Time of day: a Saturday early-afternoon kickoff matches the day-game reference and adds no commuter conflict, so this factor is neutral. Overall the factors offset, giving about the same share as EMBR day games.
Parking: almost no stadium parking, slightly scarcer than at Oracle Park, which pushes more fans toward transit (about x1.1).
Walk: 20-25 minutes uphill from DBRK, against 15 minutes on flat ground from Embarcadero, deters BART use (about x0.65).
Crowd type: a large share of the crowd is students living within walking distance, who never touch BART, so the BART share of the whole crowd is lower (about x0.8).
Competing transit: there are no Muni or ferry alternatives, and AC Transit is less direct, so BART faces less competition than at Embarcadero (about x1.25).
Time of day: the Saturday 13:00 start matches the EMBR day-game timing, so no adjustment (x1.0). The factors combine to about 0.715, rounded to 0.7.
Parking: the stadium has almost no parking, even less than Oracle Park. This pushes BART share up.
Walk: the 20 to 25 minute uphill walk from DBRK is longer and harder than the 15 minute flat walk from Embarcadero. This pushes share down.
Crowd type: a large student block walks from campus housing and never touches BART. This pushes share down.

Competing transit: Oracle Park riders are split across several downtown SF BART stations, Muni, Caltrain and ferries. At Berkeley, DBRK is the one practical BART station and only AC Transit buses compete. This pushes share up.
Time of day: a Saturday noon kickoff matches the EMBR day-game pattern, so no adjustment.
Parking: Memorial Stadium has almost no parking, at least as scarce as Oracle Park. This does not lower the BART share against EMBR and slightly supports it.
Walk: the 20-25 minute uphill walk from Downtown Berkeley is clearly harder than the flat 15-minute walk from Embarcadero to Oracle Park. This lowers the share.
Crowd type: a large student block lives within walking distance and never touches BART. This lowers the share against an MLB crowd. Alumni coming from San Francisco and the East Bay partly offset it.

Competing transit: at Oracle Park, Muni light rail stops at the gate and Caltrain is nearby, so Embarcadero captures only part of the rail crowd. In Berkeley, BART is the only regional rail and Downtown Berkeley is its stadium station. This raises the share against EMBR more than the access specialist allowed.
Time of day: a Saturday early-afternoon kickoff matches the EMBR day-game baseline. No extra adjustment is needed.
Parking: almost none at Memorial Stadium, versus little at Oracle Park, so non-students depend more on transit. This pushes the share up.
Walk: 20-25 minutes uphill from DBRK, versus a 15-minute walk from Embarcadero. Most people have no better option, so this deters only modestly. Slight downward push.
Crowd type: a large student block lives within walking distance and never uses BART. This is the strongest downward factor.
Competing transit: no Muni Metro, ferries or Caltrain-type rival, only AC Transit and rideshare. Less of the transit crowd is drained away than at Oracle Park, so this pushes up.
Time of day: a Saturday 15:00 start matches the EMBR day-game reference, so no extra adjustment.
Parking: Memorial Stadium has almost no parking, even less than around Oracle Park, so more of the non-student crowd must come by transit. This pushes the share up.

Walk: The 20 to 25 minute uphill walk from Downtown Berkeley is longer and harder than the 15 minute flat walk to Oracle Park, which pushes some riders toward rideshare or game-day shuttles. This pushes the share down.

Crowd type: Many students live within walking distance and will not touch BART, which pulls the share down. But a once-a-week college football game draws a more regional alumni crowd than an everyday baseball game, which partly offsets this.

Competing transit: Downtown Berkeley has only AC Transit buses and campus shuttles, with no Muni Metro, Caltrain or ferries as at Embarcadero, so BART captures more of the regional crowd. This pushes the share up.

Time of day: A Saturday night start means fans come from home rather than walking over from downtown jobs, as many weekday Oracle Park night fans do, so BART use rises slightly against the mostly weekday EMBR night reference.
Parking: Memorial Stadium has almost no parking, even less than Oracle Park, so more non-student fans who would otherwise drive must arrive by transit. This pushes the share up.
Walk: the 20-25 minute uphill walk from Downtown Berkeley is longer and harder than Embarcadero's flat 15 minutes. This pushes the share down.
Crowd type: many students live within walking distance and will not ride BART. Alumni and families from San Francisco and the East Bay will. This pushes the share down partly.

Competing transit: at Oracle Park, Muni Metro, Caltrain and ferries split the transit crowd. In Berkeley, BART is the only regional rail and AC Transit buses are the main alternative. This pushes the share up noticeably.
Time of day: a Saturday 19:30 kickoff matches the EMBR night reference, so there is no adjustment.
Parking: Memorial Stadium has almost no parking, versus 'little' at Oracle Park. Non-student fans from outside Berkeley are pushed onto transit much harder, which raises the share.
Walk: the 20-25 minute uphill walk is worse than the 15-minute flat walk at Embarcadero. This trims the share somewhat but does not cancel the parking effect, because there is no easier alternative.
Crowd type: a sizeable student block lives within walking distance and never touches BART. That lowers the share of the total crowd. The rest of the crowd is regional and transit-dependent.

Competing transit: at Oracle Park, Muni Metro and ferries take a large slice of transit riders. In Berkeley, BART is the only rail option and AC Transit is the only real alternative, so BART captures most non-driving regional fans. This raises the share clearly above EMBR.
Time of day: a Friday 19:30 kickoff matches the night reference. Pre-game arrivals overlap the Friday evening commute, which does not change the share much.

Parking: Memorial Stadium has almost no parking, far less than the lots around Oracle Park. For the non-student half of the crowd this pushes BART share up strongly, not mildly as the access specialist said.
Walk: 20 to 25 minutes uphill from DBRK, against about 15 minutes nearly flat from Embarcadero. This deters some riders and pulls the share down.
Crowd type: a large share of the crowd is students who walk from nearby housing and will never touch BART. This pulls the share down substantially.

Competing transit: Embarcadero splits event riders with Muni Metro, ferries and nearby Caltrain. DBRK's only real competitor is AC Transit, so BART captures more of the regional riders. This pushes the share up.
Time of day: a Saturday midday start matches the EMBR day-game reference, so it is neutral. Overall the two upward factors and the two downward factors roughly cancel, giving about 1.0.
Parking: Cal has almost no parking, scarcer than Oracle Park, which pushes the BART share up.
Walk: the 20-25 minute uphill walk is worse than Embarcadero's 15 minute flat walk. It pushes the share down somewhat, but there is no closer rail option at Cal, so riders accept it.
Crowd type: students who live nearby walk and never touch BART, which pushes the share down. On a holiday-break weekend more of the crowd is off-campus alumni and families, which partly offsets this.

Competing transit: at Oracle Park, Muni Metro at the gate, Caltrain and ferries take most transit riders, so Embarcadero gets only 2.9%. At Cal, BART is the only regional rail and the only competition is AC Transit bus. This is the strongest factor and pushes the share well up.
Time of day: a Saturday start means no after-work commuters coming from downtown offices, which help the EMBR night numbers, and weekend trains run less often. This pushes the share down modestly.
